**Android configuration changes (review PN-1).** The activity handles all of them itself. SDL can't survive a recreate: with `SDL_HINT_ANDROID_ALLOW_RECREATE_ACTIVITY` off, as it is, the new activity's `onCreate` exits the process, with no crash report and no restart. So a change the manifest doesn't list ends the run. `android:configChanges` lists every value but `resourcesUnused`, which says an activity uses no Android resources. xtask's tests hold the list to the compile SDK's, so a value a new SDK adds fails until someone considers it. [m1-exit-run.md](m1-exit-run.md) has the `wm density` check.

### 6.6 Input (`sapphire_input`, `game_ui`)

- **Default devices per platform:**
  - Desktop: KB/M plus gamepad, with glyphs following the last-used device.
  - Steam Deck: gamepad glyphs, and a 1280×800 layout check.
  - Mobile: touch plus optional gamepad. On-screen controls hide when a gamepad is used (I3: not when one connects, because the iOS simulator reports one nobody holds, and a paired pad in a bag would leave no way to play), and a finger on the glass brings them back.
- **Text input:** SDL3 text-input events show the on-screen keyboard on mobile (for name entry and the dev console).
- **As built (M1 F4):** every device is live on every platform, through one set of bindings. `sapphire_input` reports the last-used device kind with the gamepad's glyph family (the Steam Deck counts as Xbox, whose A/B/X/Y positions it shares) and how many gamepads are connected; showing glyphs and hiding on-screen controls are `game_ui`'s (M3).
- **As built (M1 F5):** `sapphire_platform` forwards text input as `Event::Text` (UTF-8 in events of at most 32 bytes, split between characters, so events stay `Copy`), only while a window takes it: `Window::start_text_input` (which shows the on-screen keyboard on mobile; a `TextInputKind` of `Verbatim`, for names, commands and codes, turns off auto-capitalization and autocorrect, `Prose` keeps them), `stop_text_input` and `set_text_input_area` for the input method. The debug console is its first user; IME composition previews are not forwarded yet.

### 6.7 Store and platform compliance

- **iOS:**
  - No JIT.
  - App Store guideline 2.5.2 on downloaded code.
  - A privacy manifest (`PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`) declaring required-reason APIs.
  - The ATT prompt only if you track users.
- **Android:**
  - 64-bit only.
  - 16 KB page-aligned `.so` files (use NDK r28+, plus a linker flag, §7.3).
  - Bump the target API level every year as Play requires.
- **macOS:** hardened runtime, codesigning, notarization.
- **Steam / Steam Deck:** controller support, legible text at 800p, and the Steam Runtime on Linux.

### 6.8 Accessibility (`sapphire_ui`, `sapphire_input`, `sapphire_render`, `sapphire_gameplay`)

- Subtitles with speaker names and a size setting.
- Full remapping, plus hold-to-toggle options.
- **Screen-shake and flash-intensity sliders.** Anime combat is flash-heavy, and these protect photosensitive players.
- Colorblind-safe attack telegraphs, with shape and icon as well as color.
- UI text scale.
- Adjustable auto-target strength on touch.

## 7. Repository layout and build

### 7.1 Layout

```
engine/
├─ Cargo.toml               # virtual manifest: [workspace.dependencies], profiles, lints
├─ rust-toolchain.toml      # pinned stable + all 7 targets
├─ .cargo/config.toml       # per-target linker flags, aliases (xtask)
├─ clippy.toml              # disallowed-methods (rule R2)
├─ deny.toml                # license policy, bans (bincode, archived crates)
├─ crates/                  # en_* engine and tool crates (flat)
├─ game/                    # game_app (bin/cdylib/staticlib), game_combat, game_characters, game_ai, game_ui
├─ platform/
│  ├─ android/              # Gradle project, GameActivity extends SDLActivity, manifest
│  ├─ ios/                  # Xcode project, Info.plist, privacy manifest, entitlements, launch screen
│  ├─ macos/                # bundle Info.plist, entitlements, icons
│  ├─ windows/              # app manifest (DPI awareness), icon, installer config
│  └─ linux/                # .desktop file, Steam Runtime notes
├─ shaders/                 # WGSL / WESL sources
├─ content/                 # source assets + .meta sidecars; third_party/ with provenance (Git LFS later)
├─ xtask/                   # build automation, layer checker (layers.toml)
├─ docs/                    # this spec, ADRs (architecture decision records)
└─ .github/workflows/
```

### 7.2 Cargo profiles

```toml
[profile.dev]
opt-level = 1
debug = "line-tables-only"

[profile.dev.package."*"]
opt-level = 3                 # deps fast, your code debuggable

[profile.release]             # internal "profile" builds with Tracy
lto = "thin"
debug = "line-tables-only"

[profile.tools]               # optimized offline cooker; fast local iteration
inherits = "release"
lto = false
incremental = true           # CI overrides with CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0

[profile.shipping]
inherits = "release"
lto = "fat"
codegen-units = 1
panic = "abort"
debug = "full"
split-debuginfo = "packed"    # PDB / dSYM / .dwp uploaded to Sentry, then stripped
```

- **Desktop dev builds** add an `sapphire_dylib` crate (`crate-type = ["dylib"]`) that re-exports the engine. `game_app` links it behind a `dynamic` feature, as in Bevy's dynamic-linking mode. This is the single biggest compile-time win.
- **Keep gameplay code in `game_app` during iteration**, because `subsecond` hot-patching only patches the top-level crate.
- **As built (M2, Z3):** neither `sapphire_dylib` nor `subsecond` exists, and `game_app` doesn't either. What keeps a code edit short is `cargo xtask run --incremental` on desktops: the `tools` profile, optimized with no LTO and incremental. A one-line edit builds in 1.4–5.5 s (5.5 s from `sapphire_math`, 22 crates), against 76–152 s under `--release`, and a whole fight's CPU frame rises from 0.54 to 0.82 ms with the GPU frame unchanged, on an Apple M5 at load about 10. A plain debug build rebuilds as quickly, at 1.44 ms of CPU and 1.6× the GPU frame. Run speed's edit reaches a fight taking input in 3.6–4.2 s from the command, with no window. The app still restarts, and a new fight starts.
- **Linkers:** keep Apple's default linker (ld-prime) on macOS. On Linux, use mold or lld. Wild is Linux-only.

### 7.3 Per-target notes

| Target | How `game_app` is built | Packaging |
|---|---|---|
| macOS / Windows / Linux | `cargo build -p <app>` (bin) | `cargo xtask bundle --platform macos` gives an `.app` with `Contents/Resources/content`. Codesigning, notarization and Steam depots come in M4 |
| iOS | `cargo build -p <app> --target aarch64-apple-ios[-sim]` (bin; SDL is statically linked) | `cargo xtask bundle --platform ios-sim` gives an ad-hoc-signed `.app`. Device signing, plus an Xcode project for sentry-cocoa, the privacy manifest and store archives, come in M4 |
| Android | `cargo rustc -p <app> --lib --target aarch64-linux-android --crate-type cdylib`, with the NDK environment set by xtask | `cargo xtask bundle --platform android`: the Gradle project in `platform/android` takes the `.so` in `jniLibs/arm64-v8a`, SDL's Java glue (synced from `sdl3-src`) and cooked content in `assets/content`. `SandboxActivity extends SDLActivity`. `cpal`'s Android context is set in M2 (plan E1) |

`.cargo/config.toml` fragment for Android 16 KB pages (**Verify** against NDK r28+ defaults):

```toml
[target.aarch64-linux-android]
rustflags = ["-C", "link-arg=-Wl,-z,max-page-size=16384"]
```

### 7.4 `xtask` commands

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask check-layers` | Enforces §4.1 and rule R8 from `cargo metadata`, and holds the simulation's crates to their dependency and clippy rules (§5.22) |
| `cargo xtask cook --cook desktop\|mobile [--only <guid/zone>]` | Runs `sapphire_pipeline` with the content-hash cache |
| `cargo xtask run --platform desktop\|ios-sim\|ios\|android` | Builds, cooks, deploys and launches, with live link enabled |
| `cargo xtask package <platform> --profile shipping` | Produces store-ready artifacts and uploads symbols |
| `cargo xtask replay [--update] [--replay <name>]` | Runs the headless combat replays in `tests/replays/` against this architecture's checksums and the zero-allocation gate; `--update` takes new values for this architecture alone (§5.22) |
| `cargo xtask replay --record <name> --scenario <name> --script <name> [--ticks <n>] [--seed <n>]`, `--list` | Records a new replay from a registered script; lists scenarios, scripts and replays |
| `cargo xtask golden [--update] [--scene <name> \| --shard <i>/<n>] [--scene-timeout <s>]` | Runs golden-image render tests, each scene with a deadline; CI splits the CPU rasterizers' scenes across runners by their CI times with `--shard` (§9) |
| `cargo xtask link status\|cvar\|push\|capture\|watch` | Live link's desktop tool (§5.29): reads a running dev build's state, sets cvars, pushes packs (only what changed), documents and WGSL sources, captures the next frame the device draws as a PNG, or watches and pushes them as they change; each command says how long the device took to answer |

- **As built (review BC-003, BC-004, BC-005, DT-007):**
  - **Info.plist:** the template's `$(NAME)` placeholders are filled in one pass and each value is escaped for XML, so a display name may hold `&`, `<` or `$(` and comes out as written. Unknown placeholders are still refused, and so are display names with control characters.
  - **iOS signing:** an exact App ID's profile is signed with its entitlements as they are. A wildcard App ID's are expanded as Xcode does: its `application-identifier`, and a keychain access group that is a wildcard of the App ID's prefix, become `<prefix>.<bundle id>`, and the rest is signed as the profile has it. No device has checked it yet.
  - **`run --platform android`** succeeds only once the app's main function returned, with status 0 where the platform layer logs it (`main returned status=<n>`). A nonzero status fails the run, naming it. A process that ends without returning fails, naming the crash's log line if there is one, and so do a logcat that exits under a running app and a device that drops. Builds without the status line fall back to SDL's `Finished main function`, which carries no status.
  - **`run --platform macos --features dev`** points the bundled app at `target/content/desktop/` through `SAPPHIRE_CONTENT_DIR`, unless the caller set it, so hot reload sees recooks. Other runs read the bundle's own copy, as players do.

## 8. CI

| Trigger | Job | Runners |
|---|---|---|
| Every PR | fmt, clippy (with R2 lints), rustdoc (warnings denied, private items included), `check-layers`, `cargo-deny`, `cargo-nextest` | Linux |
| Every PR | Build desktop binaries | macOS, Windows, Linux |
| Every PR | Compile-only builds for iOS (device, and the simulator with `dev`) and Android (with and without `dev`) | macOS (iOS), Linux (Android) |
| Every PR | Combat replay suite | macOS, Windows, Linux |
| Every PR | Golden images: lavapipe (Vulkan), WARP (DX12) and Metal (paravirtual GPU), required | Linux, Windows, macOS |
| Every PR | GPU tests: the `#[ignore]`d GPU suites on lavapipe, required; then a `dev` sandbox offscreen, driven over live link | Linux |
| Nightly | Full cook of both `desktop` and `mobile`; package all 5 platforms | Mixed |
| Nightly | Device smoke: install, boot, load a zone, 2 minutes of scripted combat, collect frame times and memory | Self-hosted Mac mini with an iPhone and an Android phone attached |
| Weekly | Thermal soak: 30 minutes of combat on Mobile-Low devices; budget regression report | Same |

**Build caching:** `sccache` 0.18, plus `cargo-hakari` to unify dependency features across the workspace.

## 9. Quality gates

A change can't merge if any of these fail:

1. **Layering and license checks:** R1, R8, and `cargo-deny`.
2. **Determinism:** all combat replays reproduce their recorded checksum for the runner's architecture, on every desktop OS.
3. **Golden images:** within `nv-flip` tolerance per backend. Rendered with the sandbox's offscreen `--capture` mode (M0), so no window is needed.
4. **Allocations:** the zero-allocation assertion (R6, simulation thread inside the fixed step) during the replay suite.
5. **Budgets:** no budget in §3 regresses by more than 10% on the nightly device run without a recorded waiver.

- **As built (M2 D2, gates 2 and 4):** CI's `Replays` job plays `tests/replays/` on Linux, Windows and macOS with no GPU: each reaches its architecture's checksums with `SimStats::allocations` at zero in every step (`cargo xtask replay`, §5.22). A test holds the gate to biting on a system that allocates, naming the first tick.
- **As built (own review DV-2, the golden gates):**
  - **Three gates.** A capture passes when its FLIP mean is at most 0.01, its 99th percentile at most 0.12 and the mean over its worst 16 × 16 block of pixels at most 0.15 (`golden::Thresholds`). The block slides over every position, so a defect reads the same wherever it lands. The whole-image gates can't see a small defect: a flat 40 px patch passed them, and on `lookdev-face` an eye is about 30 px wide. The tile gate fails a 5 px patch on the five scenes tried (they read 0.17 to 0.24; 4 px reads 0.12 to 0.17), and scattered edge flips stay under it (two flips of about 190 code values read 0.098 on CI's noisiest such tile). The p99 gate, 0.3 until then, fails a capture that lost MSAA, the render scale or the bangs' soft shadow (their siblings read 0.135 to 0.155).
  - **Noise.** Every capture of the 111 green CI runs with artifacts left (32 on `main`, 2026-10-26 to 2026-11-02, 9,216 captures per family) against the golden committed at its run's commit, through the testkit's own comparison, and seven full runs on an Apple M5 under load:

    | Family | Worst mean | Worst p99 | Worst tile |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | Metal, CI | 0.0088 (`foliage-ground`) | 0.0841 (`foliage-ground`) | 0.1215 (`foliage-ground`) |
    | Metal, Apple M5 | 0 | 0 | 0.0006 (one pixel, `lookdev-town-day`) |
    | lavapipe | 0.0059 (`shadows-faces`) | 0.0565 (`shadows-faces`) | 0.0599 (`shadows-faces`) |
    | WARP | 0.0015 (`lookdev-face`) | 0.0178 (`lookdev-face`) | 0.0384 (`lookdev-town-day`) |

  - **The closest scene** is CI's Metal `foliage-ground`, at 88%, 70% and 81% of the three gates. It doesn't wander: 103 runs drew one capture, byte for byte, which differs from the golden an Apple M5 drew as the two GPUs differ, most in a soft patch of about 15 code values at the frame's lower left. Re-baselining it from CI would take the margin back, at the cost of a golden no local run reproduces. The next closest p99 and tile are `debug-wireframe`'s on the same GPU, 0.0627 and 0.0979.
  - **What still passes.** Read as each other, 2 of the 4,465 pairs of scenes per family stay inside the gates on every family: the tier pairs `eyes-front` and `eyes-mobile` (mean 0.0096, p99 0.054, tile 0.057) and `hair-shadow` and `hair-shadow-mobile` (0.0066, 0.037, 0.045), which move a little everywhere and no more locally than lavapipe's noise. A third pair needs its own gate: `turntable-taa` and `turntable-taa-upsampled`, which differ only in the render scale the second exists to show, read 0.0085 to 0.0095, 0.066 and 0.063, inside the defaults. Those two scenes alone take a mean of at most 0.0065, above their own noise (0.0046 on lavapipe, 0.0005 on Metal, none on WARP); the mean separates them best, 0.0046 from 0.0085, where the p99 and the tile have 0.044 from 0.062. Tests hold all of this to the committed goldens.
- **As built (own review DV-8, DV-9 and DV-10):**
  - **A golden or capture that can't be compared fails its scene.** A golden of another size or colour type, or a capture the sandbox cut short, is a scene error that names the scene and keeps the capture as `.actual.png`, and the run goes on. Only a sandbox that can't start or output that can't be written stops a run.
  - **Scripted runs refuse what they don't know.** `--capture` and `--bench` exit with an error, naming them, on arguments they don't know, so a misspelled pin can't render another picture and bootstrap a golden of it. The windowed app and `--offscreen`, whose arguments the OS and SDL may add to, log a warning.
- **As built (review BC-008 and BC-107, the golden harness):**
  - **Deadlines.** Each scene's sandbox writes its output to `target/golden/<scene>.log` (a file, not a pipe: the crash monitor inherits it) and has a deadline, the testkit's `--scene-timeout` (900 s by default, which `cargo xtask golden` passes on; the slowest scene takes about 130 s on WARP). A scene past it is killed, fails as timed out with the last 40 lines of its log, and the run goes on to the next. Only the sandbox is killed, with `SIGKILL` (`TerminateProcess` on Windows), and its crash monitor exits when its lifeline closes. A hung scene leaves no minidump: a `SIGABRT` first would need a signal API that std lacks, and Windows has no counterpart. A test runs the runner against a fake sandbox (the test binary run again, with a fake crash monitor of its own) that hangs, or writes over 100 KiB to each of stdout and stderr and stalls: both fail within the deadline with their logs kept, both monitors exit, and the scene after them, which writes twice that and exits, passes.
  - **Times.** Every scene's line gives its wall time, and `target/golden/timings.json` lists them (scene, family, seconds and status: `ok`, `updated`, `no-golden`, `failed`, `error` or `timed-out`), rewritten after each scene so a cancelled job keeps what it had. CI uploads both with the captures. In CI, the minidumps are gathered when a golden job fails or is cancelled (as a job past its time limit is), and the serial-passes replay runs only when it fails: a new push cancels a PR's run in progress, where the replay would cost every golden job minutes, and a hung scene now fails at its deadline. Each step has its own time limit.
  - **Shards by cost.** `--shard` splits a family's scenes by their CI times, a table in the testkit (`scenes/costs.rs`: the medians of four `main` runs' times on lavapipe and WARP, read from their logs) chosen by the backend `SAPPHIRE_GPU_BACKEND` forces: costliest first, each scene joins the slice with the least so far, and each slice keeps the list's order. A scene missing from the table counts as the costliest; tests check that every shard count CI uses (and 1 to 6) holds every scene exactly once, a scene without a cost included, and that the table names no scene that is gone. Any other backend deals the scenes out in turn, as before. On the same runs, the slowest shard's scenes go from 10.4 to 8.2 minutes on lavapipe (two shards) and from 9.3 to 7.9 on WARP (four); each held-out run, split by the other three's medians, gains 1.6–3.2 and 0.8–1.8 minutes. Refresh the table from the jobs' `timings.json` as scenes change.
- **As built (review BC-001 and BC-002, GPU tests and `dev` builds in CI):**
  - The `GPU tests` job runs every `#[ignore]`d GPU test of `sapphire_render`, `sapphire_rhi`, `sapphire_world`, `sapphire_debug` (DV-10: the overlay's gesture toggle, DT-002) and the sandbox's `dev` half on lavapipe (`--tests -- --ignored --test-threads=1`), with the golden jobs' environment; it is required. On Metal (Apple M5, `SAPPHIRE_GPU_DEBUG=none`) the suites take about a minute. A test a CPU rasterizer can't run skips itself, naming the adapter and why; none does so far. WARP runs the same suites in its own workflow, `gpu-tests-warp.yml`, on pushes to `main` and on PRs that edit it: about 31 minutes of tests after a cold 18-minute build, longer than a PR's other checks together. The four temporal AA tests that failed on its first trial were test limits, not D3D12 faults: a flat sky one half-float step from an sRGB rounding boundary, an exact-zero velocity against the target's smallest step, and a line width 0.5% over its limit. `sapphire_rhi`'s Apple-only surface test runs only on Macs, locally. `sapphire_crash`'s ignored test isn't a GPU test.
  - The same job runs a `dev` sandbox offscreen on a private port and drives it with live link's tool: its status, a cvar, a capture and a document that doesn't parse, which the app must refuse and count; then it must quit with status 0 on `SIGTERM`. The iOS job builds the simulator with `dev` (the device build stays the shipping one), and the Android job bundles a `dev` APK after the default one.

## 10. Milestones

These windows are rough estimates for a small, senior team. A solo developer should expect them to stretch.

| Milestone | Window | Build | Exit test |
|---|---|---|---|
| **M0 Bring-up** | Months 0–2 | Workspace, layer rules and CI on 3 OSes. `sapphire_platform` (SDL3 main callbacks) and `sapphire_rhi` (Metal / Vulkan / DX12) on all 5 platforms. Skeletons of `sapphire_core`, `sapphire_math`, `sapphire_jobs` and `sapphire_time`. Tracy, `sapphire_crash`, and iOS Xcode / Android Gradle packaging. A glTF character with a basic two-tone character shader and hull outline. | **The same commit** runs the outlined two-tone character at target fps on Mac, Windows, Linux (including Steam Deck), an iPhone and an Android phone. Background → foreground survives on both phones, and a forced crash reaches Sentry from every platform. |
| **M1 Data path** | Months 2–6 | ECS, reflection and serialization; the `sapphire_assets` runtime. `sapphire_pipeline`: glTF / FBX, `ctt` BC and ASTC, meshopt, packs, content-hash cache, hot reload. Renderer v1: frame graph, compute skinning, forward lighting, shadows, the anime character recipe (track C), the world look (time of day, sky, fog, ambient probes, stylized environment shader) and the post stack. VRM import and anime map tools, `sapphire_input`, `sapphire_debug`, live link, golden-image tests. The plan is [m1-plan.md](m1-plan.md). | Editing a ramp, material parameter or time-of-day key shows up on desktop *and* phone without a restart. The look-dev scene meets the tier budgets on all 5 platforms. Golden images pass on 3 backends. |
| **M2 Combat slice** | Months 4–10 | `sapphire_anim` (our own runtime, inertialization, IK, spring bones), `sapphire_physics`, the combat core, party swap, camera director, one enemy AI, audio (`kira`), VFX v1, touch controls, live tuning, and the timeline editor v1. The plan is [m2-plan.md](m2-plan.md). | One character against one enemy **feels right** with a gamepad on desktop and with touch on a phone. Replays are deterministic in CI, and Mobile-Low holds 30 fps while thermally throttled. **This is the go/no-go gate.** If tuning still feels slow, take the off-ramp in the report: move gameplay and tools to Godot with gdext, and keep the Rust systems. |
| **M3 World and tools** | Months 8–18 | Zones and transitions, navigation, sequencer and dialogue, Luau, `sapphire_ui` with the HUD and menus, saves, localization, the editor document model with undo and play-in-editor, and the pipeline (PSO) inventory. | A zone with 3 encounters, a boss authored with no Rust changes, one cutscene, and a full HUD and menus in 2 languages, all on 5 platforms. |
| **M4 Ship readiness** | Month 12 onward | PSO warm-up, signed chunk manifests and `sapphire_patch`, quality tiers with dynamic resolution and thermal handling, the symbol pipeline, accessibility, and store compliance. | Zero shader hitches in a scripted playthrough. Patches download only changed chunks. Builds pass TestFlight, Play internal testing and Steam review. |

**M0 status (2026-10-24):**

- **Done and verified on 3 of the 5 platforms.** The same code renders the outlined two-tone mannequin at 60 fps on macOS (Metal), the iOS 26.3 simulator (Metal) and the Android 16 emulator (Vulkan through MoltenVK). It survives background → foreground on Android, and a forced crash leaves a valid minidump on macOS.
- **Since then (2026-10-24):** CI runs on GitHub, and Windows and Linux build and pass their tests there. Tracy is verified: a trace from the sandbox on the headless iOS Simulator records every engine zone and wgpu's. Release builds link on every Apple target (thin LTO used to drop a symbol SDL needs).
- **Deferred by decision (2026-10-24):** crash upload. Nothing needs it yet, so the Sentry backend was removed from `sapphire_crash`, which halves its dependency tree. Minidumps are still captured and kept for the next launch (the newest 8 runs' reports, §5.2), and the backend comes back from git history once there is a project to send reports to.
- **Still open for M0 exit:**
  - A run on Windows and Linux hardware.
  - A physical iPhone, which needs a signing identity.
  - A physical Android phone.

**M1 exit run:** [m1-exit-run.md](m1-exit-run.md) is the procedure for exit test 1 and the phones' budget measurements: the six edits (ramp, character and environment materials, time-of-day key, cvar, WGSL), the commands per target (desktop headless, iOS Simulator, Android emulator, an Android phone through `adb reverse`, an iPhone through `cargo xtask run --platform ios` and `iproxy`), what to measure and record, and what only a device can prove. It was rehearsed on 2026-10-26 on everything but the phones (§5.29).

**M1 status (2026-10-27): done, pending devices.**

- **The decision.** There is no test hardware for now: no iPhone or Android phone, and no Windows or Linux machine with a GPU. So M1 is called done with its device checks still owed, and work pauses before M2. [m2-handoff.md](m2-handoff.md) is what M2 inherits: what was deferred, the device checks, what it builds on and the known risks.
- **Exit test 1, iteration: verified on the desktop, the iOS Simulator and the Android emulator.** From the look-dev hero shot, a ramp, a character material, an environment material, a time-of-day key, a cvar and two WGSL sources were each pushed over live link, seen in a capture, undone and seen gone (X2's rehearsal on 2026-10-26, and the desktop again on 2026-10-27 with C7 and the look-dev stage's own day; [m1-exit-run.md](m1-exit-run.md), §5.29).
  - Push to reply took 2 to 138 ms on every target, except a cold shader compile. Content adds its cook, 0.5 to 1 s. On the desktop, hot reload applied a saved document in 0.12 to 0.30 s and content in 0.66 to 0.79 s with its cook.
  - Shaders now build off the frame thread (M1 A8 follow-up 2, live link protocol 3; §5.12, "Materials, shaders and PSOs"). In the rehearsal a cold compile held the frame for 1.7 to 3.5 s. Now no frame is held: a cold `post.wgsl` or `anime_character.wgsl` push shows after 1.8 to 2.1 s on the desktop, with no frame over 15 ms, and after 2.3 to 2.7 s on the iOS Simulator, with no display-link tick missed. The emulator wasn't run again.
  - The first cook after editing a WGSL source or the default day takes 0.5 to 1.1 s, where it took 22 to 72 s (M1 A8 follow-up, §5.27).
- **Exit test 2, the look: the scene is built; its budgets are measured on this Mac only.**
  - The scene is X1's look-dev stage (`--look-dev wide|hero|sky|street|face`): the VRM character with an authored ramp, ILM and SDF face map, in a Jinzhou-style town of the project's own with a few CC0 pieces, through the stage's own day and night with the post stack on. It was judged against Wuthering Waves reference frames kept outside the repository. Its goldens and benches keep W5's AO off, and the town has no probe grid, so W5's probes and AO show in the courtyard's `ambient-*` scenes instead, and P3's screen effects in the `effects-*` scenes.
  - On the Apple M5 (release builds at 1080p, AO off), the wide and hero shots take about 4.2 ms of GPU time on Desktop-High (X1 part 2f; C8's adoption added 5 to 24 µs to the main pass) and the street 6.6 ms (part 2b). With the Mobile tiers' settings, at 1280×590 or 1080p, Mobile-High took 1.1 to 4.3 ms and Mobile-Low 1.0 to 3.3 ms (parts 2a to 2c). That is far inside the GPU frames of §3.1 (8–12, 13 and 26 ms), but the M5 is none of §3.1's reference devices.
  - The iOS Simulator held the hero shot at 30 fps on Mobile-Low, every frame 33.3 ms. The Simulator and the emulator draw on the Mac's GPU, so neither says what a phone does. Windows and Linux render the look-dev scenes only on CI's software rasterizers, for goldens.
- **Exit test 3, golden images: passing on all three backends.** There are 95 scenes, each with its own golden on Metal (this Mac, and `macos-26` in CI), lavapipe (Mesa 26.1.3) and WARP 1.0.21. The default gates are a FLIP mean of 0.01, a 99th percentile of 0.12 and a worst 16 × 16 tile of 0.15 (§9).
  - Every pull request runs them all, all required: lavapipe in two shards, WARP in six and Metal in one job (Q6; when its informational flag came off, 239 of its 288 runs since 2026-10-25 had succeeded and 48 had been cancelled, with none failed).
  - At 87 scenes, each lavapipe and WARP shard took 11 to 14 minutes with its build, and the Metal job 17 (CI run 40493256145, `main` at bc3389c).
- **Still open, all of it needing devices:**
  - Exit test 1 on an iPhone and on an Android phone ([m1-exit-run.md](m1-exit-run.md)). `cargo xtask run --platform ios` has never run on a phone; it needs the user's Apple signing identity.
  - Exit test 2's Mobile budgets on phones, measured throttled (§3), and the tier a real phone's memory selects.
  - F7's ProMotion check and F8's 90 and 120 Hz phone check (§6.2).
  - Windows and Linux hardware, still open from M0 (above), the Steam Deck included.
  - The open questions that need devices (§11): Q3 (the Steam Deck: native or Proton), Q4 (Windows' default backend), Q5 (on-tile MSAA on Mali, Adreno and Apple GPUs, and Metal binary archives), Q9 (device floors, throttled) and Q14 (Android pre-rotation).

**M2 exit run:** [m2-exit-run.md](m2-exit-run.md) is the procedure for all four exit tests: a fight on a gamepad, the feel reviews' sheet with which file and field changes what, a fight on a phone, timing a saved move, checking replays by hand and a phone's soak with its pass and fail lines. Everything that needs no window and no phone was rehearsed on 2026-11-02, and its last section says what ran.

**M2 status (2026-11-02): built, and not judged.** "Done, pending devices" is true of exit tests 2 and 4 and of test 1's touch half. It isn't true of test 1 on a gamepad, which needs no device beyond a pad and has simply not been done.

- **The decision that's open.** M2 is the go/no-go gate, and [m2-go-no-go.md](m2-go-no-go.md) is what the maintainer decides from. They were away for the whole of M2 and told the run to carry on without asking, so every package was built, phase 5 included, with none of the three feel reviews behind it, against the plan's order ([m2-plan.md](m2-plan.md) §5). [m3-handoff.md](m3-handoff.md) is what M3 would inherit.
- **Exit test 1, feel: not judged by anyone.** Nobody has played this fight, heard its sounds, felt its rumble or opened the timeline editor. **Feel review 3 is the plan's real go/no-go check, and it hasn't run.** What's verified is that the fight runs:
  - On a desktop, no window has ever shown it, because agents may not open one. Tests run 4,400 ticks through the renderer offscreen, holding three fights to a headless run's checksums (G6). The review made a played fight hold the pointer, pause on lost focus and show its pause (§5.18), with tests of what decides that and only SDL's source for what SDL does.
  - The window's loop has run on a headless Android emulator, played by real multi-touch events to a win and a loss, and on an iOS simulator with no touch at all (I3). That found a debug-build panic on a window's first step, fixed since. A pad has only been synthetic.
  - The pillars' stand-in numbers (plan §2) hold where they exist: a press moves the character on tick 1 (G1) and every move by 0.18–0.68 m by tick 2 (O3), one cue fires a hit's effects in one tick (E3), cancel and perfect-dodge windows are covered by replays on the test moves but not on O3's document (G4), the camera keeps both fighters inside 90% of the frame through a scripted fight (G5), and spring bones run on every tier (N5). `TargetingWeights::TOUCH` chooses who the director frames in a fight played on touch, and with one enemy only its reach shows. They catch regressions and say nothing about feel.
  - Whether the motion is good enough to judge by is the largest open question. There's no animator: poses are solved from targets (O3), and locomotion and reactions are retargeted chibi clips (O2). Both packages call their results first drafts.
- **Exit test 2, iteration: holds on the desktop, an emulator and a simulator; a phone is owed.** Numbers from 410cf24b, before the review's fixes. A real save of `player.moves.ron`, moving `light_1`'s timing, against a running `--arena --fight` with a press every half second, the next attempt plays it in a median of 487 ms, a 90th percentile of 765 ms and at most 1,183 ms over 25 warm rounds, and a fresh process's first edit in a median of 556 ms and at most 585 ms over 4, against 2 s (Apple M5, release `dev`, Desktop-Low at 1280×720, load 11–17). Up to 500 ms of each is the wait for the press, and each is to the first move that starts on the new data, the edited one in 86 of 124 rounds. Over live link it's a median of 436 ms and at most 1,338 ms on the Mac, 259 ms and 906 ms on an Android emulator over 20 rounds, and 357 ms and 843 ms on an iOS simulator over 16, against 5 s. Neither is a phone: both draw on the Mac's GPU, and the tool's 21–28 ms says nothing of a phone's USB or Wi-Fi. The character's graph takes a save and a push too (134 ms and 7 ms on 7a28c828), and the enemy's comes through a cook. The same bytes are no edit, a length or a misspelt field is refused by name, a bad document keeps what's playing, a cook that started before a save leaves the save playing, and the next fight starts from the edit, tick for tick what a headless run of those edits plays (G6, `tests/live_tuning.rs`, in CI on lavapipe). Tuning that isn't data pays a rebuild and a new fight, and the controller's numbers are code. §7.2's `sapphire_dylib` and `subsecond` were never built. A one-line edit builds in 76–152 s under `--release` and 1.4–5.5 s under `cargo xtask run --incremental` (Z3), which costs about 0.3 ms more CPU in a frame.
- **Exit test 3, determinism: passing, enforced on every pull request.** 11 replays reach their architecture's checksums with no heap allocation in a step (§9, gates 2 and 4), in CI's required `Replays` job on `ubuntu-24.04`, `windows-2025` and `macos-26`, Linux and Windows against one file. Run by hand here, all 11 pass with a mean step of 2.3–4.6 µs and a longest of 255 µs over two runs (Apple M5, `cargo xtask replay`'s optimized `dev` build). Five sessions played on an emulator and a simulator replay on the Mac to the checksums those devices logged (four from I3, one from Z3), and a script's fight ends on one checksum on the Mac, the emulator and the simulator. The review's fuzz held too: 51,678 swaps, 542 forced, 156 parties down, 6,609 perfect dodges, 6,035 counters and 1,007 defeats across 200 seeds × 3 swap rates at 4,000 ticks, each run twice, deterministic with no allocation, and live bytes flat over 400 restarts and 2 hours of ticks. That's arm64 only. Cross-architecture equality isn't asked for: arm64 and x86-64 keep a file each. **Since about 12:30 UTC on 2026-11-02 GitHub's macOS runners have been out,** so `macos-26`'s jobs (this one, tests, Metal goldens and iOS builds) were verified for each landing by a local stand-in running the same commands on this Mac. CI's own should run again when runners return.
- **Exit test 4, budget: open, and needs a phone.** Z1's fight bench has every row of §3.2 and §3.3 on an Apple M5 at the tiers' sizes and cooks (§3.5): under budget except post on Desktop-Low while a fused screen effect is up (0.78 ms against 0.7), nothing allocated in a step, nothing built after a fight's first frame, 350 MB on Mobile-Low, and memory and frame times flat over 17.8 minutes at a true 30 fps. **None of that answers the test,** which is Mobile-Low on a phone, thermally throttled, after 15 minutes. The route is ready: a script fights unattended on a phone, and `frame stats` now carries the OS's thermal state (Z3). It ran on an emulator for 8.5 minutes, 19 fights on one checksum, which proves the route and times nothing.
- **The review.** Five agents who hadn't built the code reviewed it after the packages landed and found 31 bugs in code CI passed, all fixed, 29 with a test and two in the editor's window by reading. [m2-go-no-go.md](m2-go-no-go.md) says what that means for the evidence, and [m3-handoff.md](m3-handoff.md) has what they left open and the rules they made.
- **Still open:**
  - Feel reviews 1, 2 and 3, and the go/no-go.
  - A gamepad on a desktop, with real rumble. Sound on any speaker. The pointer and focus by hand ([m2-exit-run.md](m2-exit-run.md)).
  - A phone: touch by thumb, exit tests 2 and 4, audio on a device, and §3.5's list. iOS has never had a touch. No phone has run anything in M0, M1 or M2.
  - M1's device checks, all still owed (M1 status above), Q3, Q4, Q5, Q9 and Q14 among them.
  - End-to-end input latency, press to glass (§4.2).

## 11. Open questions to resolve

| # | Question | Resolve by |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 | ~~Does the SDL3 entry flow work from Rust?~~ **Answered in M0:** yes. `SDL_RunApp` runs on the iOS simulator, and an exported `SDL_main` with SDL's JNI symbols links for Android (see Android results in ADR 0002). | M0 spike |
| Q2 | ~~Android 16 KB page alignment~~ **Answered in M0:** NDK r28+ defaults already produce 16 KB-aligned `.so` files; the rustflag in `.cargo/config.toml` is belt and braces. | M0 |
| Q3 | Steam Deck: native Linux build, or the Windows build under Proton? Prefer native. | M0; still open at M1's close, for want of a Deck (§10, M1 status) |
| Q4 | Which Windows default backend, Vulkan or DX12, based on Intel / AMD / NVIDIA driver testing? | M1; still open at its close, for want of Windows hardware (§10, M1 status) |
| Q5 | wgpu on mobile and Apple: on-tile MSAA / transient attachments, timestamp queries inside passes on Apple GPUs, Android pre-rotation, Metal binary archives. **Partly answered in M0:** MSAA and depth are transient attachments, and Apple GPUs report the memory saving; the M5 has no timestamps inside passes. The iOS simulator lacks base vertex / first instance, indirect execution, cube arrays and comparison samplers, so the CPU-driven draw path avoids them (ADR 0002). **M1 plan:** mobile AA is 4× MSAA kept in tile memory through `TRANSIENT_ATTACHMENT`, to be measured on Mali and Adreno; one-pass deferred stays impossible until wgpu gets input attachments (#10148). **M1 R7:** the phone tiers keep 4× MSAA as transient attachments, held there by a GPU test; the measurement on Mali, Adreno and Apple devices moves to M2. | M1; the device measurements are still open at its close (§10, M1 status) |
| Q6 | ~~Do hosted CI runners expose a GPU for Metal golden images?~~ **Answered (M1 plan):** yes. GitHub's macOS arm64 runners expose Metal as "Apple Paravirtual device", and wgpu runs its image tests there on every PR (shader validation is broken there; 3 vCPU). Goldens run per PR on lavapipe, WARP and `macos-26` Metal. | M1 |
| Q7 | ~~Does ozz-animation-rs cover offline animation building?~~ **Answered ([m2-plan.md](m2-plan.md) §3):** it has no offline tools, still needs nightly Rust at HEAD and has no stable path, so `sapphire_anim` is our own runtime with our own cooker, with no C++ in the pipeline. | M2 |
| Q8 | ~~FMOD license tier and cost; if blocked, the `kira` backend becomes primary.~~ **Answered ([m2-plan.md](m2-plan.md) §3):** blocked for a public repository, so `kira` is primary, as the maintainer confirmed. | M2 |
| Q9 | Device floors (A14 / Snapdragon 865 / 6 GB), measured while thermally throttled. | M2; still open at its close, for want of a phone (§10, M2 status) |
| Q10 | iOS policy on downloadable scripts and content: legal and App Review guidance. | Before any live-service plan |
| Q11 | Current App Store and Play size limits, which shape the install-time vs CDN content split. | M4 |
| Q12 | ~~Android crash capture~~ **Answered in M0:** there's no workable monitor process on Android. `sapphire_crash` writes an async-signal-safe signal record and chains to `debuggerd`; symbolicated native crashes come from Sentry's Android NDK SDK in the Gradle project. | M0 |
| Q13 | ~~iOS frame pacing: engine-owned `CADisplayLink` or present-interval pacing?~~ **Answered in M1 (F7, ADR 0003):** an engine-owned `CADisplayLink` at the tier's rate drives SDL's own main-callback functions; a pure pacer holds back early ticks and measures intervals. Decided text, simulator results and the device check that remains are in §6.2. | M1 |
| Q14 | Android pre-rotation: wgpu doesn't pre-rotate, so SurfaceFlinger rotates our landscape buffer on portrait-native phones. Measure the cost on real devices before choosing whether to render pre-rotated. | M2; still open at its close, for want of a phone (§10, M2 status) |
